plan: This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since payment equals the second-highest bid (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value exceeds the price I'd pay) and avoid losses. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $3, I'll bid $3 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and overpaying. If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. With no history to analyze (this is the only round), I'll bid exactly my true value of $24.

This is a second-price auction where the winning bidder pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. With a value of $11, bidding $11 ensures I maximize expected profit - I'll win whenever the second-highest bid is below $11 and pay exactly that amount, capturing the surplus.
